newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses end mixed, dollar up on mark.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses end mixed, dollar up on mark.

text.p: Key European bourses put on a mixed performance on Wednesday, failing to hold early record or near-record levels but reviving by the close.

Paris stocks reversed by more than two percent from early all-time peaks to close more than one percent lower amid concern over company taxes. Frankfurt scored a record close but this was below early intra-day peaks.

The London stock market, Europe's biggest, ended a roller-coaster day with healthy gains, reassured by details of the new British Labour government's first budget after jitters ahead of the event had sent it lower.
Finance minister Gordon Brown was still speaking as business closed but investors welcomed a surprise two percentage point cut in corporation tax and forecasts of low inflation and falling borrowing.

On the currency market, the dollar regained some strength after being hit by a rush into the yen following news of the flotation of the Thai baht. It also advanced to a new 40-month high against the weak mark.
"Breaking 1.75 marks was a tough nut to crack. We are above that level now and it should provide support," said a senior trader at a British investment bank.

The British pound also moved above 2.91 marks for the first time in five years on market expectations that fiscal tightening would not prevent higher interest rates. It ended around 2.91 versus 2.8880 at the previous close.
Speculative selling, meanwhile, sent gold to its lowest level since March 1993.

New records early in the day on the Frankfurt, Paris and Milan bourses, adding to a strong advance the previous day, were prompted by gains on Wall Street on Tuesday and strength in the dollar, good news for exporters.
But on Wednesday the Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue chips had lost around a quarter of a percentage point by the close of European trading.

The Paris bourse, having gained 1.4 percent to a new peak, took a big hit from late morning after government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann confirmed that the new Socialist-led coalition was studying new company taxes.

Shares in Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel were briefly suspended limit-up after jumping more than 20 percent on news that France and Britain could extend its licence to 99 years. Eurotunnel ended Paris trade up 9.4 percent at 7.55 francs after an early high of 8.40.
The London stock market had followed a 2.7 percent leap on Tuesday by rising to within five points of its record level on the FTSE 100 index in early trade.
Then, led by futures, it slid back in hectic and nervous pre-budget dealings before rising again on the budget news to end the day virtually half a percent higher.

But traders said the market's final verdict was yet to come and abolition of the tax credit on dividends claimable by pension funds, a key factor in equity valuations, could still undermine share price gains.
"The markets are up and down like a yo-yo, we don't know what to make of it yet," said one dealer.
German shares finished bourse floor trade at a record close but the 30-share DAX index was below an earlier intra-day high.
"The pretty strong dollar has really given this market a fresh outlook," said one Frankfurt trader. "The outlook for now is for consolidation before making another attempt to go higher."
The mark retreated after news that German industrial production fell 0.2 percent in May and more hints that the planned single European currency could be soft.
The yen, meanwhile, became a safe haven after the Bank of Thailand said it was dropping its pegged rates system against a basket of currencies and allowing the market to set rates.

"Whenever a developing currency is allowed to float, there is always some fear in the market and that causes a capital outflow, and in the Asian region the safe haven is obviously the yen," said Alessandra Stagliano, economist at Daiwa Europe.
In reaction the dollar sank to a session low of 114.15 yen but later recovered as the surprise wore off, while ending European business below its previous yen close.

Looking slightly further ahead, currency traders did not anticipate any change in interest rates from a meeting of the U.S. central bank's Federal Open Market Committee which ends on Wednesday, with news due at 1815 GMT.
Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International, said U.S. non-farm payrolls data, due on Thursday, could be of more interest to traders.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 114.44 yen and 1.7515 marks, compared with 114.90 and 1.7421 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 23.1 points or 0.49 percent at 4,751.4, having earlier hit 4,791.1, just below its all-time high of 4,796.0 reached in mid-June.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed 34.59 points or 1.17 percent lower at 2,909.45 after an earlier record 2,986.09.

FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade up 34.91 points or 0.91 percent at a new record close of 3,854.76 after an all-time record 3,871.13 earlier. The IBIS DAX for after-hours electronic trade finished up percent at 3,867.53.
PRECIOUS METALS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
Gold ended London business at $332.35 an ounce, up from a 4-1/4 year low fixing of $331.45 in the morning but below $333.65 at Tuesday's London close. Silver was down one cent at $4.66.
